content: Patients taking medications that are known to prolong the QTc interval should undergo regular monitoring with ECGs and electrolyte assessments. Voriconazole can increase the levels of ospemifene by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and close monitoring are advised when these drugs are co-administered. Oxaliplatin may elevate voriconazole levels or effects through other mechanisms, necessitating careful monitoring. Initiating therapy with QT-prolonging drugs in patients already on such medications requires ECG monitoring to detect potential changes. Oxcarbazepine reduces voriconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy adjustments and close monitoring. Both ozanimod and voriconazole can prolong the QTc interval, and their combined use should be approached with caution and close monitoring due to potential additive effects on heart rate. Ozanimod should generally not be started in patients concurrently taking QT-prolonging drugs with arrhythmogenic properties. Similarly, paliperidone and voriconazole both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Voriconazole increases panobinostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and the starting dose of panobinostat should be reduced to 10 mg when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Voriconazole also increases pantoprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Additionally, voriconazole elevates parecoxib levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism, and paricalcitol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, both requiring careful monitoring.
